title: Session-fanout SDK and lazy-tooling PRD (draft)
content:
TL;DR
This is a working PRD for a new Hosted API surface that enables: (a) session-level fanout where a single logical session can produce multiple independent "mini-streams" (progressive outputs, tool call lanes, and diagnostic channels); (b) a lightweight tool-call preflight manifest that allows client SDKs to express expected tool inputs and preferred fallbacks; and (c) a compact structured-output framing model (delta frames + patch merge semantics) that keeps streaming low-latency while enabling robust client-side reconciliation.

Why this?
We keep seeing customers build multi-tool orchestrations and interactive UIs that need: low-latency partial outputs, orthogonal channels (tool calls vs content generation), and resumability across unreliable network paths. Current streaming CRs are single linear flows — mixing tool-calls and text causes awkward client-side heuristics and manual parsing. Session-fanout makes the server explicitly emit lanes and small frames clients can handle deterministically.

Goals
- Reduce client parsing complexity for mixed outputs (text + tool-calls + metadata)
- Keep median time-to-first-token same as current streaming API (< 100ms for standard models)
- Allow safe resumability of sessions at the lane/frame granularity (resume from last committed frame)
- Provide an ergonomic SDK surface for TypeScript/Python that makes fanout lanes feel like first-class async iterables
- Provide a preflight tool manifest: client says "I plan to call tools A,B; prefer sync x over y" and server can annotate compatibility and capacity hints

Non-goals
- This PRD does not attempt to replace long-running workflow engines. Fanout is for single-session interactive flows (<30m).
- Not adding large new server-side orchestration (no persistent worker-per-tool here). Initial implementation will route to existing tool adapters.

User scenarios (sketch)
1) Collaborative editor with inline tool suggestions: editor opens a session; model streams a prose lane and a side lane with suggested code edits (tool-call lane). The client renders prose immediately and shows patch frames that can be applied incrementally.
2) Agent UI with tool preflight: client declares tool intents with a manifest; server confirms compatibility and emits a cost/latency hint for each tool. Agent UI can decide to suppress heavy calls.
3) Poor-net resume: mobile client loses connectivity; on reconnect it requests frames since last-committed sequence number and the server resumes all lanes that still exist.

High-level API surface (ideas)
- POST /v1/sessions -> returns session_id and primary_stream_url
- Client opens a single streaming connection (HTTP/2 or WebSocket) and receives a multiplexed stream with lane headers
- Each frame: { lane: string, seq: int, type: enum "text"|"tool_call"|"tool_result"|"meta", payload: bytes (utf8 / json), commit: boolean }
- Resume endpoint: GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/resume?since_seq={n} -> server streams frames > n
- Preflight: POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/preflight with manifest of planned tools and example payloads

Protocol details — mini-streams and framing
- Lanes: logical named channels (e.g., main, tool-translation, tool-search, diagnostics)
- Frames are small (<=4KB recommended) to keep RTTs small; longer outputs are auto-chunked at token boundaries
- Each lane maintains its own monotonic seq counter; sequence numbers are per-lane and globally unique tuple (lane, seq)
- Commit semantics: clients acknowledge frames they have persisted (ACKs). Servers tag frames with commit:false until a frame is marked commit:true. Resume uses last-ack (per-lane) to trim replay.
- Control frames: lane-open, lane-close, lane-move (rename), heartbeat, quota-hint

Structured output model (delta frames + patch merge)
- Instead of emitting full JSON blobs repeatedly, we send small delta frames: { op: "replace"|"patch"|"insert", path: "/items/3/title", value: ... }
- Clients apply patches using a deterministic merge rule; server may emit occasional snapshot frames marked commit:true for easier recovery.
- Tool results are typed and include a schema id; schemas are lightweight JSON-Schema / Protobuf-lite references that can be looked up from a registry (hosted or client-cached).

Tool-calling UX: preflight + manifests
- Manifest: client provides a list of tool descriptors (name, expected_payload_shape_hint, preferred_sync_async, privacy_level).
- Server response: compatibility map (supported|unsupported|quota-limited) + per-tool estimated latency buckets + opt-in telemetry flags.
- Preflight enables the server to choose to synthesize smaller partial results instead of firing expensive tool calls, or queue tool calls behind a low-priority lane.
- Tool calls emitted in stream as explicit tool_call frames with a call_id. tool_result frames reference call_id. This avoids ambiguous parsing.

SDK ergonomics (core principles)
- Lanes as async iterables: SDK exposes session.openLane('main') which returns an AsyncIterable of typed frame objects in TypeScript and an async generator in Python.
- Backpressure primitives: SDK exposes ack(seq) and fast-forward(seq) for clients that want to commit locally without roundtrip ACKs. SDK implements auto-ack heuristics for small-output UIs.
- Builder pattern for manifests: new SessionBuilder().withTools([...]).withResumeToken(token).start()
- Declarative reconnection: SDK tracks lastCommittedPerLane and can transparently call resume endpoint and rehydrate iterables.
- Convenience typed frames and runtime validation: SDK auto-validates tool_result frames against cached schema and surfaces clear typed objects to callers.

Observability / telemetry
- Emit per-frame telemetry: lane, seq, latency tokenDistance, tool_call_id, model_version, worker_host (redacted)
- SDK will surface backpressure metrics and report when auto-ack heuristics suppressed ACKs (helps diagnose lost-commit bugs)

Security and privacy notes
- Preflight manifests are advisory; they may contain user-intent hints and could be PII. Default retention for manifests: 7 days unless customer opts into longer retention.
- Tool payloads marked privacy_level: "sensitive" must be forwarded only to private deployments or dedicated lanes with encryption at rest.

Compatibility and migration
- Backwards compatibility: server will continue to support the current linear streaming protocol. New sessions can opt-in via session.create param: streaming_mode: "fanout-v1".
- Gradual rollout plan: beta with SDKs then public opt-in then default for new workspaces after 90 days.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should seq numbers be global across lanes (single incrementing counter) vs per-lane? Per-lane reduces contention but complicates global ordering for audit logs.
- Commit model: do we require explicit client ACKs (safer) or allow server-side commit heuristics? Hybrid seems necessary.
- How large should frames be (4KB default) — needs tuning against tokenizer boundaries and network MTU.

Operational considerations
- Worker-level routing: lanes may be routed to different workers (text on gpu pool, tool calls on cpu pool). We need to ensure resume semantics across worker restarts.
- Cost accounting: map per-tool-lane token and external API calls into the usage pipeline so customers see per-lane costs in Console.

Next steps (short-term)
- Tech spike: implement a middleware multiplexer in our serving runtime to produce lane-framed output (ENG-1428) — 2 engineer-weeks.
- SDK spike: small TS prototype showing lanes as async iterables and resume semantics — 1 engineer-week.
- Security review of preflight manifest retention policy — security ticket.
- UX session with solutions eng + a pilot customer (agent UI) to validate manifest ergonomics.

Appendix: quick example (pseudo)
- Frame stream (human-readable):
  lane="main" seq=1 type=text payload="Hello" commit=false
  lane="suggestions" seq=1 type=tool_call payload={call_id: "c1", tool: "refactor", args: {...}} commit=false
  lane="suggestions" seq=2 type=tool_result payload={call_id:"c1", patches:[{op:"replace", path:"/0/body", value:"..."}]} commit=true

Notes-to-self:
- Keep naming distinct from other streaming proposals; emphasize lanes+commit model and preflight.
- Coordinate with infra (routing) and billing (per-lane cost tags).

References / links:
- design notes: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/HOST/Session+Fanout+Notes
- spike ticket: ENG-1428
- SDK prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api-prototypes

(Iterate — this is intentionally a sketchy PRD to gather product/infra/eng feedback. Put comments in the Confluence mirror and ping #hosted-api for sync)
